DESTRUCTIVE_MISTAKE_AND_FULL_RECOVERY.what_happened: editPage on a live Telegraph article requires the full node list as the new content. I read the page with getPage, which returned ok=true but content: [] - an EMPTY array. I did not treat that empty array as the danger it was, and sent editPage with only one new paragraph. That replaced the entire article body.
DESTRUCTIVE_MISTAKE_AND_FULL_RECOVERY.damage_confirmed: served HTML contained only my single added paragraph - 0 characters of original body
DESTRUCTIVE_MISTAKE_AND_FULL_RECOVERY.recovery: the full original 11-node body was still in scripts/publish_telegraph_gpsr_takedown.py as the BODY constant. Extracted it by exec'ing the module source with the publish call cut out and an assertion that createPage is absent, then rewrote the page via editPage.
DESTRUCTIVE_MISTAKE_AND_FULL_RECOVERY.residual_harm: none. No permanent loss. Recovered from our own repo, not from a third party.
DESTRUCTIVE_MISTAKE_AND_FULL_RECOVERY.THE_RULE_THIS_SHOULD_HAVE_PRODUCED: getPage returning content: [] means 'this page's body was NOT read', not 'this page has no body'. Never call editPage on a page whose content came back empty - that is indistinguishable from overwriting it. Assert the node list is non-empty first, every time.
